clue.text: So taken aback after blunder in examination

indicators.note: after places the turned So behind the word for blunder

parts.note: a blunder is a trip, a slip or stumble

indicators.note: taken aback means the word So is turned round to face backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is startled after making a mistake in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns SO into OS, which goes after TRIP. The TRIPOS is the honours examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the final honours degree exam at Cambridge, so it is a kind of university examination.

clue.text: Controller employed to size things up

definitions.meaning: one who governs, a monarch or sovereign
a measuring stick used for gauging lengths

explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign controls a realm, and a straight-edged measuring stick is used to gauge sizes.

clue.text: Poor writer samples work of Edgar Allan

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author of tales of mystery
a taster is a sample, a small trial portion

explanation.surface: A hack dips into the stories of Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of' is a link here; POE comes from his first names and TASTER from 'samples'.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trivial or inferior verse, a would-be poet.

clue.text: One should have views on this railway

definitions.text: One should have views on this railway

parts.words: One should have views on this railway
parts.note: a railway along which passengers enjoy fine landscape, also the old name for a fairground roller coaster

explanation.definitionFit: A scenic railway is a fairground ride, and the word itself means having attractive landscape views.

clue.text: Strange rays come from this American plane

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters of rays come are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd rays emerge from a US aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges RAYS COME. 'Plane' looks like an aircraft but is the plane tree: Americans call their plane tree a sycamore.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the plane tree (Platanus) is commonly called the sycamore.

clue.text: Deputy having a little brief authority

parts.note: a second is a brief moment, a little time
having authority means being in command

explanation.surface: A deputy given a small, short-lived amount of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' links: having authority is being IN COMMAND, and a brief little while is a SECOND.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer next below the commander, who takes over in their absence, is a deputy.

clue.text: Hide evidence of the prodigal's feast

definitions.meaning: in the parable of the Prodigal Son the fatted calf was killed for his homecoming, leaving its pelt

explanation.definitionFit: A young bovine's pelt is a leather, and it would be left over after the fatted calf was slaughtered for the Prodigal Son.

clue.text: Novelist with a lapidary style?

definitions.meaning: A. E. W. ..., author of The Four Feathers
lapidary means relating to stone, so one who works in stone

explanation.definitionFit: A. E. W. Mason wrote adventure novels, and a stoneworker's craft is literally lapidary.

clue.text: New market, say, for a reconditioned car racket

indicators.note: reconditioned means rebuilt, so the letters of car racket are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh marketplace could hide a scam involving reconditioned cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconditioned' rearranges CAR RACKET. 'New market' is Newmarket, the English town famous for horse racing, split to look like a new marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket in Suffolk is a famous horse-racing course, an example of a racing circuit.

clue.text: Manual instrument sharpened to cut things out

definitions.text: Manual instrument sharpened to cut things out

parts.words: Manual instrument sharpened to cut things out
parts.note: a hand-held writing tool with a point, used by an editor or censor to mark passages for deletion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut things out' sounds like a blade, but the tool is a pencil an editor uses to strike out text.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor's coloured pencil is the traditional tool for marking cuts and censorship in a text.

clue.text: Get rid of old wine

definitions.meaning: a dry white wine from Spain and the Canaries drunk in Shakespeare's day, as Falstaff's favourite

explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an employee is to give them the push, and sherry-like Spanish white wine of the 16th century bore this name.

clue.text: Rustic orders car to take Diana out

indicators.note: orders here is a verb telling the letters of car to be arranged afresh
out signals that car and Diana are put out of their original shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A country type tells a car to collect Diana and go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' and 'out' both call for a rearrangement of CAR and DIANA together.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia was the idealised pastoral region of Greece, so its adjective means pastoral or countrified.

clue.text: Foreign money put away by council

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
to put food away is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A council stashes away currency from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' looks like saving money, but here it means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a governing or advisory assembly, a kind of council.

clue.text: Scrap sunless holiday

indicators.note: sunless says the letters spelling the word sun are removed from the holiday

parts.note: Whitsun is the Christian festival of Pentecost, traditionally a British holiday

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of a holiday without sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunless' is read literally: take SUN out of WHITSUN, the Pentecost holiday (a bank holiday in Britain).
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit', so it means a scrap.

clue.text: Jumps on bed before church — childish game

parts.note: hops are small jumps
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Bouncing on the bed before Sunday service is a child's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'before' just order the pieces: HOPS, then COT, then CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game of hopping through squares chalked on the ground.

clue.text: Native girl takes husband to the isle

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A local woman brings her husband over to the island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' and 'to' simply string IRIS, H and MAN together. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native, here a person born on the island of Ireland, an islander from the Emerald Isle.

clue.text: Master's voice heard in grave situation

parts.note: a head is a headmaster, and the 's gives head's
tone of voice, its quality or pitch

explanation.surface: His master's voice is heard at a serious moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in' links the pieces to the definition. 'Grave situation' sounds like a crisis, but it is where a memorial stone is placed.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial stone stands at the head of a grave, so that is its location.

clue.text: Miss Spenlow inefficient but charming

indicators.note: in places the name inside the word for efficient

parts.note: able means capable, efficient
Dora Spenlow, David Copperfield's first wife in Dickens

explanation.surface: Dickens's Dora Spenlow was hopeless at housekeeping but delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'inefficient' as 'in efficient': DORA goes in ABLE. Dora Spenlow, Copperfield's child-wife, was famously hopeless at housekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is lovable, delightful, charming.

clue.text: Random spread of crop aids

indicators.note: spread of suggests the letters of crop aids are scattered about into a new order

explanation.surface: Farm fertilisers scattered haphazardly over the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread of' rearranges CROP AIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic happens at irregular, scattered intervals, so it is haphazard.

clue.text: Symbol the essence of Tutankhamen

indicators.note: the essence is the inner core, so the letters are taken from inside the pharaoh's name

explanation.surface: A sign that captures the spirit of the boy pharaoh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the essence of' takes letters from the heart of TutANKHamen.
explanation.definitionFit: The looped cross was the Egyptian hieroglyph for life, held by gods and pharaohs.

clue.text: Make protest through the post

definitions.meaning: to stand outside a workplace demonstrating during a strike
a pointed stake, as in a fence

explanation.definitionFit: Strikers demonstrate at the gates, and a pointed wooden stake forms part of a fence.

clue.text: Duck being escort all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters of escort are mixed up

explanation.surface: A duck accompanying someone wanders everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges ESCORT.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck of northern coasts.

clue.text: Kind of seat that can go either way

definitions.text: Kind of seat that can go either way

parts.words: Kind of seat that can go either way
parts.note: a hinged seat that can be up or down, as in a cinema row

explanation.walkthrough: 'Either way' means up or down: the seat is hinged so it flips up when nobody sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-up seat folds up when unoccupied, as in a theatre or cinema.

clue.text: Support for what Canute could have said

parts.note: King Canute, in the legend, ordered the tide to halt; main is an old word for the sea
stay is the command to stop or hold back, given to the waves

explanation.surface: A prop for the words the king might have spoken to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Canute (Cnut), an 11th-century king of England, is said to have commanded the incoming tide to stop: 'Main, stay!' where main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is a chief support, originally the rope steadying a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Walk briskly behind her?

parts.note: to walk briskly is to march, and the month named for that comes just before her in the calendar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk briskly' is March; 'her' is the month that follows March, given a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The month after March is also used as a girl's name, so she follows the brisk walk in the calendar.

clue.text: Pace for the favourite's come-back

indicators.note: come-back says the letters of the favourite's word return in the opposite direction

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, and the 's adds an S: pet's

explanation.surface: Walking speed matters for the favourite's return to form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come-back' turns PETS (pet's, the favourite's) round. The apostrophe s here supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single stride, and so a measure of pace or gait.

clue.text: VDU in the classroom

parts.note: a visual display unit, the screen of a computer, here thought of as the old wall-mounted surface a teacher writes on

explanation.walkthrough: VDU stands for visual display unit, a computer monitor; the classroom's original display surface is chalked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's dark chalk surface is the original visual display at the front of a schoolroom.

clue.text: He would not mind being unemployed

definitions.text: He would not mind being unemployed

parts.words: He would not mind being unemployed
parts.note: mind is read as tend or look after: when out of work this herdsman has no flock to tend

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not mind' reads as 'not care', but it means he would have nothing to look after.
explanation.definitionFit: A herder of sheep minds a flock, so without work there is nothing for him to mind.

clue.text: Voice of youth

parts.note: the high singing voice of a boy before his voice breaks

explanation.definitionFit: A boy chorister sings in the highest register, the part named for the top line of choral music.
